description.narrative: The objective of the Nagaland Health Project for India is to improve health services and increase their utilization by communities in targeted locations in Nagaland. There are two components to the project, the first component being community action for health and nutrition. This component is designed to empower communities to oversee, manage, and improve HNP services and their utilization. An incentive strategy will be used whereby funding will be nutrition-related services and practices. In turn, communities will use the incentives for activities and investments that are important to them and have potential impacts on health and nutrition. The component will have a major focus on knowledge and skill building of Village Health Committees and other stakeholders at the community level, including women's groups and Village Councils. Village Health Committees will be supported in identifying existing gaps, determining the most suitable approaches to address these gaps, developing action plans, and operationalizing those plans. Finally, the second component is the health system development. This component will support improvements in the management and delivery of health services, including both facility-specific and system-wide investments.
To improve health services and increase their utilization by communities in targeted locations in Nagaland.

condition.narrative: Finance Agreement :Agreements with Village Health Committees | Description :The Project Management Unit shall make a portion of theproceeds of the Financing available on a grant basis to each selected Village Health Committee by means of an Incentive Agreementexecuted between the Project Implementing Entity, through the Project Management Unit, and the selected Village Health Committee,all under terms and conditions set forth in the Project Operations Manual. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement :Use of Health and Nutrition Incentives | Description :Terms and conditions set forth in the Project OperationsManual shall include, inter alia, the Village Health Committee's obligations to: demonstrate on a quarterly basis, the achievementof the performance targets proposed in its respective Health and Nutrition Action Plans; to utilize the Health and NutritionIncentives in accordance with sound technical, financial, environmental and social standards and practices and with theAnti-Corruption Guidelines; to refrain from using the Health and Nutrition Incentives for the financing of any IneligibleExpenditure; to carry out all procurement related to activities to be financed by the Health and Nutrition Incentives inaccordance with the provisions set forth in the Project Operations Manual; and to maintain cashbooks and registers recordingfinancial transactions to demonstrate meeting the requirements of the Project Operations Manual, the resources, expendituresand full utilization of the Health and Nutrition Incentives by the Closing Date. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

title.narrative: People who have received essential health, nutrition, and population (HNP) services

comment.narrative: Please note there was a mistake reported in the ISR from May 2023 on this indicator. First, "People who have received essential HNP services" indicator is to report a cumulative number. Second, the cumulative value of this indicator was 836,419 instead of reported 1,423,667 in the May 2023 ISR. Third, the incremental value of this indicator between November 2022 and May 2023 ISR was 142,678.

Community health workers (ASHAs) in targeted communities supplied with complete kits (Percentage)

comment.narrative: While the end of the project target for this PDO indicator is 100 percent, the indicator has improved from 92.9 percent in October 2022 to 93.5 percent in March 2023, hence showing an increasing trend despite not achieving the March 2023 target.

title.narrative: Target villages where a village health and nutrition day was organized in the previous month (Percentage)
Mothers who delivered in the previous 6 months in targeted communities who had at least 4 antenatal care check-ups (Percentage)

comment.narrative: The current Health Management Information System (HMIS) does not capture the four Antenatal Care (ANC) services (PDO#5) from both public and private health facilities, hence the information from the external verification agency of rounds 6 and 7 has been used to monitor PDO#5 as it is more representative than the routine reporting system (e.g., HMIS). This was done both in the October 2022 and April 2023 Implementation Support Missions.
